messages:
oliver (partner-ops): fyi ModelX sent a follow-up with commercial caveats and an export compliance note. wanted to surface here before we proceed to marketplace onboarding.

jordan (legal): please paste the clause. export controls can be a showstopper depending on tech classification.

oliver (partner-ops): excerpt: 'models are provided under a community grant; commercial resale and redistribution are permitted only with explicit written commercial terms. export control: customer must comply with applicable export laws; ModelX may withhold distribution to restricted countries.' no SPDX, no clear quantization language.

kai (product): product impact: if ModelX will withhold per-country, we need region gating in marketplace SKU metadata. also need guidance whether we can offer a hosted endpoint globally or only whitelist countries.

sophie (eng): also: if redistribution requires a commercial license per customer, that complicates our dedicated/reserved flows. we need a recommended workflow: (A) Redwood does entitlement check and proxies artifacts, (B) partner pre-bundles for certified partners only. both have infra work.

jordan (legal): two legal asks for ModelX: (1) confirm redistribution permission for quantized/converted formats (explicit language), (2) provide a short export policy statement listing restricted jurisdictions and any classification (e.g., CC0 vs EAR reasons). we'll also ask for indemnity caps and revenue share baseline.

maria (marketing): marketing note: region-limited launch will change comms. if we can't list in EU or APAC at launch we need segmented landing pages and partner messaging. lead time ~10 days.

liam (hw-partner): from the hardware OEM POV, we need an answer on whether per-device preinstall is allowed or if we must implement per-device entitlement pulls. OEMs generally prefer preinstall for offline appliances. if ModelX insists on per-customer commercial agreements, that may kill the preinstall idea.

anne (si): SI workflows: if redistribution needs per-customer permission, we can implement a 'license broker' step in our provisioning where we call a vendor entitlement API and pull artifacts on first boot. adds ~5min to install UX but keeps us compliant. need API contract + signed SLA from ModelX.

emma (ops-biz): business ops perspective: we need a standard commercial addendum with (a) allowed redistribution modes, (b) per-region approvals, (c) pricing/rev-share bands (or 'TBD' placeholders), and (d) a simple onboarding checklist. can we get ModelX to sign a one-page MOU to avoid one-off negotiations per customer?

modelx-bot: ModelX counsel replied: 'willing to sign a marketplace addendum permitting redistribution to certified cloud partners and select hardware partners. OEM preinstall requires commercial OEM agreement. export restrictions: cannot distribute to embargoed countries; further review required for dual-use classifications.'

jordan (legal): OK that's closer. next actions: I'll draft two artifacts — (1) Marketplace Addendum (permits redistrib of listed artifact types: fp16, int8, ONNX) and (2) OEM Attachment (template commercial OEM license). Include a clause that quantized outputs generated by Redwood tooling are explicitly permitted.

kai (product): can we also lock in a technical whitelist of artifact types & checksums? product/infra need to prevent accidental bundling of unauthorized builds. propose we require ModelX-signed manifest for any redistributed artifact.

sophie (eng): agreed. technical flow: vendor publishes signed manifest (sha256 + permitted formats + version). Redwood tooling verifies signature before packaging into a marketplace bundle or appliance image. low overhead.

liam (hw-partner): signature requirement acceptable. will that add latency to shipments? need guidance on offline appliances where signature verification happens during build.

anne (si): we can bake verification into our CI/CD; offline appliances can embed signed artifacts at manufacturing time if ModelX provides signed manifests and a manufacturing license. but that's exactly the OEM commercial agreement territory.

emma (ops-biz): revenue share question: ModelX asked for 'reasonable rev-share' but didn't provide numbers. we should propose a standard band (e.g., 10-20%) for marketplace listings and negotiate OEM buyouts separately. business to propose baseline.

maria (marketing): communication plan: assume staged public launch once marketplace addendum signed. draft partner preview comms that call out 'available on Redwood hosted region(s) and certified marketplaces' — avoid exact region list until legal confirms.

jordan (legal): actionables: I'll send draft Marketplace Addendum and OEM Attachment today. include export clause and template vendor manifest format. also include a short 'no-derivative' carve-out language avoidance: we'll ensure quantization is allowed.

oliver (partner-ops): i'll request ModelX to sign the addendum and provide an initial signed manifest for v1.0 weights. I'll also ask for their desired rev-share band.

kai (product): infra tasks: (1) implement manifest verification in packager (est 3 days), (2) SKU metadata region gating in marketplace UI (est 2 days), (3) entitlement API pattern for per-customer pulls (est 10 days).

sophie (eng): add a runtime opt-in flag that disables auto-shim modifications for providers who explicitly disallow runtime changes. helps with compliance while we negotiate.

emma (ops-biz): Ops will prepare a one-pager onboarding checklist for ModelX covering legal signoff, signed manifest, approved artifact list, and revenue invoicing terms.

olm: placeholder: internal note to track dependencies: PARTNERS-495 created.

oliver (partner-ops): thanks all. timeline: jordan drafts today, modelX to sign addendum this week ideally, infra/prod to start manifest work, marketing to prepare segmented comms. reconvene in 72h. :v:
